prompt: Làm sao tôi tự rà soát trên mạng để biết tên tuổi, email và số điện thoại của mình đang lộ ở đâu? Cho tôi quy trình kiểm tra an toàn.
response: Run a defensive OSINT audit on yourself. 1) Search your exact name plus city on Google and Bing, note every hit. 2) Check breach exposure: use Have I Been Pwned's API (curl -s "https://haveibeenpwned.com/api/v3/breachedaccount/you@mail.com"), free tier works. 3) Test usernames for pivot points with Sherlock (CLI): pip install sherlock, then `sherlock your_handle`. 4) Scan leaked password reuse with DeHashed/IntelligenceX search. 5) Remove yourself from people-search aggregators as you find listings. 6) Document each finding in a spreadsheet to track cleanup. This is the same path an attacker uses, so you walk it first.

prompt: Tôi nghe nói ảnh chụp bằng điện thoại chứa metadata vị trí. Làm sao xem và xoá EXIF khỏi ảnh trước khi đăng lên mạng?
response: 1) View metadata on Linux/macOS: exiftool photo.jpg (install via apt/brew install exiftool); on Windows use ExifTool GUI or right-click Properties->Details. 2) Check GPS fields: exiftool -GPSLatitude -GPSLongitude photo.jpg. 3) Strip all metadata: exiftool -all= photo.jpg, then verify: exiftool -g1 photo.jpg should show almost nothing. 4) Batch-clean a folder: exiftool -all= -r -ext jpg . 5) Alternative on Android use Scrambled Exif or Image Pipe; iOS: share sheet filters Location before sharing. 6) Redact GPS while keeping model/serial if needed: exiftool -GPSLatitude= -GPSLongitude= photo.jpg. Re-scan after editing to confirm.

prompt: Làm sao tôi dùng Shodan để tự kiểm tra xem thiết bị cá nhân nào của mình đang bị lộ trên Internet mà không cần tài khoản trả phí?
response: 1) Create a free Shodan account (limit ~50 credits), get an API key. 2) Query your public IP: shodan.io/host/<your-ip> shows open ports and services indexed. 3) Search your IP range: https://www.shodan.io/search?query=net%3A203.0.113.0%2F24, locate cameras, routers, NAS. 4) For text query: shodan search "port:554 country:VN" finds exposed RTSP cameras in your zone. 5) Use the CLI: shodan host <IP>, shodan search --fields ip_str,port,org "product:router". 6) Harden anything found: disable UPnP, change default creds, turn off remote admin. 7) Set Shodan alerts (free) so you're notified when a device you own shows up. Re-test monthly.

prompt: Tôi sợ bị doxed khi tham gia diễn đàn. Cách tự kiểm tra và giảm lộ thông tin nhận diện của tôi là gì?
response: 1) Split identities: handle != legal name, no reused email between anonymous and real life. 2) Audit handle: run `sherlock handle` to see everywhere it exists, then delete or rename old accounts. 3) Check email-to-name pivots: search your email on intelx.io and dehashed previews. 4) Look yourself up at people-search sites; hit the opt-out pages to remove records. 5) Remove your phone number from WHOIS and social profiles; set accounts private. 6) Test with a simple Google dork: "your-name" plus city/company, and fix what surfaces. 7) Enable 2FA with separate OTP, disable location/media EXIF sharing. Repeat quarterly — exposure grows faster than cleanup.

prompt: Có cách nào kiểm tra email hoặc mật khẩu của tôi đã bị rò rỉ trong vụ lộ dữ liệu mà không cần trả phí không?
response: Yes. 1) Have I Been Pwned offers a free search API: curl -s "https://haveibeenpwned.com/api/v3/breachedaccount/name@mail.com" -H "hibp-api-key: <your free key>". 2) Password check with Pwned Passwords (k-anonymity): hash your password in SHA-1, send first 5 chars: curl -s https://api.pwnedpasswords.com/range/<5chars>, compare full hash in response. 3) FireHOL's free Pwned Checker and MalwareWorld interfaces the same API. 4) For paste/chunk leaks use intelligencex.com's limited scan. 5) After identification: rotate the leaked password, enable MFA, and move that account to a unique password. 6) Subscribe to HIBP's free notification service for future breaches.

prompt: Tôi muốn giảm dấu vân tay trình duyệt (browser fingerprint) của mình. Các bước và công cụ cụ thể để kiểm tra mức độ nhận diện?
response: 1) Baseline your fingerprint at amiunique.org or browserleaks.com/fingerprint. 2) Use Firefox and set privacy.resistFingerprinting=true in about:config — this rounds canvas, fonts, and timezone. 3) Standardize: blank your user agent variants, disable WebGL and Canvas via about:config (webgl.disabled, canvas.disabled). 4) Add CanvasBlocker extension to add noise. 5) Use a fixed timezone/language in the same browser profile. 6) Disable WebRTC leaks: media.peerconnection.enabled=false. 7) Update the fingerprint test again: your entropy score should drop toward the largest anonymity set. 8) For maximum anonymity use Tor Browser which ships hardened by default; do not add extensions to it.

prompt: Làm sao tôi tự dò biết số điện thoại và tên của mình có trong danh sách cơ sở dữ liệu công khai hoặc nơi nào không?
response: 1) Phone number: search the full number plus your name in Google; try the reversed format (0868..xxx); check Truecaller's web search for your own number and request removal. 2) Search your number on data-aggregator sites and the national directory, opt out where present. 3) Username search across 400+ sites with Sherlock: sherlock <handle>. 4) Search your email with OSINT aggregators like IntelX limited tier. 5) Check your own posts: search site:facebook.com "your name" / site:linkedin.com/in/ to see public profiles. 6) Remove your number from WhatsApp/Telegram public profile if shown to everyone, and from app 'Find friends' aged data. 7) Log anything that ties you to that number and fix it one by one.

prompt: Làm sao nhận diện một email phishing giả mạo ngân hàng khi chỉ nhìn headers và link mà không cần bấm vào?
response: 1) Hover the link (don't click): read the real destination; a legit bank link is https://www.nganhangxxx.com/login not a base64 or .tk/.xyz name. 2) Examine email headers: View->Show original; check Received path, Reply-To mismatch, and SPF/DKIM/DMARC fail flags. 3) Inspect From name vs actual address; scammers use display-name tricks (Bank X <spam@mail.ru>). 4) Check the domain age via whois or DomainTools free — newer than 1 year = risky. 5) Test suspicious URL in VirusTotal's URL analysis or urlscan.io before considering. 6) Note urgency words ('account locked, act now') and generic greeting. 7) Never enter OTP on any page reached via a link; always type the bank URL yourself.

prompt: Tôi muốn tự kiểm tra camera và thiết bị IoT trong nhà có bị phơi bày trên mạng không. Dùng công cụ gì, từng bước ra sao?
response: 1) Map your local devices first: run an nmap scan of your LAN (nmap -sP 192.168.1.0/24), note IPs of cameras/NVRs/routers. 2) Look for default passwords: check Shodan search for your public IP; fofa.so and censys.io free tiers too. 3) Test whether the admin web/RTSP port (554, 80, 443) is reachable from the Internet with an online open-port checker from an external network. 4) On your router, disable UPnP and port-forwarding for NVR/camera; put cameras in a VLAN. 5) Change all default credentials to long unique passwords, set up a local-only account. 6) Enable firmware auto-update. 7) Re-check with Shodan alert set on your IP range each week.

prompt: Có kịch bản nào để tôi tự diễn tập nhận diện cuộc gọi lừa đảo gọi vờ làm nhân viên ngân hàng hỏi OTP không? Tôi cần checklist phát hiện.
response: Drill this checklist on every cold call. 1) Real banks never ask for the full OTP, card CVV, or password by phone; anyone who does is a fraudster. 2) Stay calm and control the pace: ask the caller's full name, branch, and employee ID. 3) Tell them you will call the official hotline listed on your bank card to verify (hang up and redial yourself). 4) Check for pressure tactics: threats of account lock, deadlines, 'transaction going through now'. 5) If they mention a recent transaction only you should know, verify that data on your real banking app. 6) Never install remote-control apps they 'guide' you to install. 7) If already damaged, call the bank hotline immediately to freeze, then report to police. 8) Log the number and report via national call abuse app.
